teaser: Traffic spikes and your sync Flask service chokes; you move TicketFlow to AsyncAnthropic, lock down secrets and let the SDK retry for you.

scene.title: Traffic is spiking and the sync service is timing out
scene.sceneHtml:
TicketFlow: Week 2

Traffic is spiking. Your synchronous Flask service is blocking the event loop on every Claude call, and requests are timing out. The team needs concurrent ticket processing. You migrate to AsyncAnthropic and integrate it into the async Python stack.

takeaways: In async services (FastAPI, async workers) use AsyncAnthropic: await messages.create() and asyncio.gather() to run calls concurrently.
Never commit API keys to source or Git; load them at runtime from environment variables or a secrets manager (AWS, GCP, Vault).
The SDK retries 429/500/503 and timeouts automatically with exponential backoff up to max_retries; do not write manual retry loops.
Route errors by impact: 429/500/timeouts are warn and retry; AuthenticationError (401) is critical and pages on-call; 400 means fix code.
